classes.class_name: S0 (layout only: bars, edge shading, rivets, seams)
S (layout + procedural wear, 5 noise layers + grain; NOT traced)

derivation_ceiling: Reference height = grey brightness of the colour, blurred 0.7 dots, through a 12-point steep tone curve (grey 50-72 -> height 100-170): mean error 5.0 levels of 255 (correlation 0.989; a 3D colour lookup does no better, 5.8). Reference normal = Sobel slope of the 8-bit height, strength 5 (5.7 degrees from the uploaded height, 6.7 degrees from the predicted height). So even a perfect colour picture cannot get below height error 5.0 / normal angle 6.7 degrees; the tier 'exact' (needs 6 and 4) is unreachable through derived maps, 'close' is reachable (and reached by L).
variation_result: 8 new tiles from sample_description(seed 1..8) (5.0-5.9 KB each, new layouts: strap/brace/seam/rivet placement drawn from ranges measured on the reference, plus the S wear layers with new seeds), baked through the same generator. texture_compare 'same kind': mean 0.569 (0.525-0.603; fitted S on the reference layout 0.523, L 0.498). Against the reference at pixel level they are poor as required: SSIM 0.39-0.42, edge skill 0.00-0.02, Delta E 13-14, tier none for all 8. Between each other: mean colour difference of a pair 18.7 levels, pair SSIM mean 0.399 (max 0.421). Bake 26-67 s each (colour only, 8 samples, loaded machine). Contact sheet: variations/contact_sheet.png (copy in guide_pictures/variations_contact_sheet.png). Honest gap: 0.57 is far below the 0.99 of a reshuffled copy; the tiles lack the reference's clumping by panel and long drips, and layouts are slightly busier. Two sampler rounds were needed (first round made braces poke out of small panels and too many straps).
area_result: One 2 x 2 area of NEW unique content: sample_description(seed 21, tile_multiple=2), 9.2 KB, baked at 2508 dots (298 s with all maps on a loaded machine). Seams: wrap-around jump ratio 1.016, middle cross lines 0.985 and 0.863 (1.0 = no seam). Quadrant-pair SSIM 0.45-0.51 (different content); strongest autocorrelation repeat (shift > 60 dots) only 0.236 (bars / rivet rows, not copied areas). Picture: guide_pictures/area_2508_seed21.png; numbers: area/summary.json. Not tested: anything bigger than 2 x 2.
resolution_result: Same description at 512 / 1254 / 2508 dots (8 samples, all maps). L: 12.6 s / 26.8 s / 90.0 s; SSIM vs reference 0.731 / 0.756 / 0.757, edge skill 0.43 / 0.58 / 0.58. S: 13.7 s / 54.8 s / 293.9 s; same-kind 0.373 / 0.523 / 0.524. What changes is time (noise-based S grows 5.4x for 4x the dots, L 3.4x); scores at 2508 equal those at 1254 (they are measured after shrinking to 1254), no new detail appears because the description holds detail to about 1254 dots, outlines just get smoother stair-steps; 512 scores lower only because the comparison tool blows the picture up. Painted shapes and shader-noise features-per-tile are resolution independent. Details: resolution/resolution_tests.json.
transfer_result: Ship's HULL PLATES (not given), description only, generator code unchanged: transfer/make_hull_plates.py (43 lines) writes description/hull_plates.json (17.9 KB): 6 wide overlapping plate bars with the same shared edge profiles, 3 butt-joint bars per row shifted by half a plate every second row, two rows of small rivets per plate (same rivet picture, radius 7.5), blue-green paint colours, same three wear layers with new colours/stretch (rust streaks 130 x 14 features, rust ~12%, stronger rivet attraction); thresholds set by the same calibrate_wear.py. About 6 tool calls end to end; 20 s calibration + 80 s bake (19 074 shapes, all maps). Judged by eye only (no reference): stepped plates, lap shadows, rivet rows, joints and rust streaks look right; paint tone is too wavy, rust too sparse, rivets too brown at the laps. Picture: guide_pictures/transfer_hull_plates.png; notes: transfer/transfer_notes.json.
geometry_route_verdict: Tried the real-geometry route (generator/metal_geometry_route.py): Geometry Nodes group 'Metal bar' = Curve Line + Quadrilateral profile + Curve to Mesh (+ Transform), used 21 times; rivets = point cloud + Instance on Points of an 8-sided Mesh Cone + Realize Instances + Set Material. Whole scene builds and is photographed (height + true normal) in 1.3 s versus 14-45 s for the painted route. But real-geometry height does not match the reference height (correlation 0.07; straight-line fit gain 0.06), because the reference height is just colour brightness. With the L colour: derived height error 17.1 (best fit 16.6) / normal 10.62 deg (close); geometry only 32.4 / 13.25 (layout); mixing 20/40/60% geometry: 18.3/20.8/24.2 and 10.68/10.97/11.50 (no gain, slightly worse). Verdict: derive maps from colour for matching this reference; use the geometry route only when real raised parts (displacement, 3D mesh) are wanted.
what_each_layer_bought: Plate + bar faces (3.6 KB): SSIM 0.613, edge skill 0.00, normal 13.3 - flat structure only
+ bar edge shading from measured edge profiles (4.1 KB): SSIM 0.649, edge skill 0.15, height error 32.3 -> 28.1
+ 33 rivets (8-slice dome picture) + 3 seam lines = S0 (4.8 KB): SSIM 0.655, Delta E 8.6, edge skill 0.23
+ 88 traced patches (16 KB): edge skill 0.30; 275 patches (32 KB): first tier 'layout' (0.35)
M = 841 patches (65 KB): SSIM 0.692, edge 0.42, height 22.3, normal 12.1 (tier layout)
256 KB (5392 patches): tier 'close' (SSIM 0.740, edge 0.55, height 17.9, normal 11.0); L = 9155 patches (413 KB): SSIM 0.756, Delta E 4.9, edge 0.58, height 16.6, normal 10.6

Procedural wear instead of tracing (S, 6.3 KB): dot-for-dot gets WORSE than layout alone (SSIM 0.655 -> 0.479) but 'same kind of surface' rises 0.20 -> 0.52; the two comparison tools want different layers
Each doubling of traced bytes buys about +0.01 to +0.03 SSIM and +0.05 to +0.07 edge skill; it never saturates below the size limit; tracing is a coded copy of this tile's rust, not a description
lessons_that_transfer: Fit the derivation rule (colour -> height/normal) first and write down its error: it is the ceiling and tells you which tier is reachable (metal: close, never exact)
Roll the reference by half a tile and look for its own seam before tracing it; heal a 14-dot strip and trace on a wrap-padded copy (tiling score 0.30 -> 0.84 at no pixel cost)

Layout by numbers: dark-line detector + rotate-and-count scan for bars, template matching for repeated objects (Hough circles found nothing), median edge profile along the whole bar using only the less rusty half of samples

Half-dot trap: traced outlines run through dot centres and 'dot i' spans i..i+1; fixing registration + growing outlines by 0.5 dot lifted edge skill 0.526 -> 0.581 and SSIM 0.716 -> 0.759; a fast OpenCV preview that includes boundary dots hid it - always compare the preview with the real render
Blender tessellate_polygon silently mis-filled 396/8687 outlines; use a slab (horizontal-strip) fill that handles touching outlines; only refuse outlines with proper crossings
Rank traced patches by gain per byte (error removed, edge dots x3) on a coarse palette: 8 colours beat 16 and 24 at a fixed size; only trace what the layout does not already paint

Procedural wear = seamless 4D 'donut' noise + Map Range + constant Color Ramp; calibrate every threshold from the noise's own quantiles so each colour covers the share you ask for; match patch size/anisotropy/clumping statistics first (my first pass was far too fine)
A 'cover everything' colour layer hides earlier layers; brightness layers must Multiply (128 = no change)

Texture scores are noisy and the spectrum measure is normalised by total energy: tuning one layer moved other sizes and made the score worse (0.516 -> 0.41); check per-size spectrum differences before changing a layer, and stop when two rounds gain nothing
Two comparison tools are needed: tracing wins dot-for-dot, statistics win 'same kind' - never mix random wear under traced patches
Make the sampler from ranges measured on the reference PLUS rules that stop ugly layouts (braces only in roomy near-square panels, 2 straps each way mostly); expect two rounds of look-and-fix
Transfer is cheap if the generator reads everything from the description: hull plates took one 43-line script, one calibration, one bake
Real geometry (Curve Line/Instance on Points) is 10x faster to build but only useful when real raised parts are wanted; here the reference height is just colour brightness
known_gaps: The two long thin scratches of the reference and the two overlapping rivets at its seam are not reproduced in S/M/L (only partly through traced patches)
S and the sampled tiles lack the reference's long vertical rust drips from every rivet/edge (only one thin drip layer) and its clumping by panel; 'same kind' is 0.52-0.60, far from 0.99

L is tracing (a coded copy of this tile's wear), not a description; M and L keep a small leftover seam (texture_compare seam ratio 1.34/1.37 vs reference 2.02, tiling 0.84/0.81) although half-tile test passes

M and L audit: one 2400-corner outline and the audit's grid rule refused them at first; fixed by capping outlines at 120 corners and storing outlines in chunks of 60 (same order) - the chunking works around the audit rule rather than changing data (largest list 241 numbers, 413 KB vs 4.7 MB picture); reported in guide section 10
S seam test shows mean difference 3.2 levels (0 per cent over 40) because float rounding flips noise thresholds; control is 19.5
Grain bug found late (used 3D shape height); variation tiles baked before/after the fix differ in grain only; hard (1-sample) vs smooth (8-sample) edges not re-tested after the half-dot fix
Roughness/metallic/ao maps are made but not scored (no reference); ao is a blur difference, not ray-traced; 'exact' tier unreachable by design (derivation ceiling)
analysis_findings.md could not be written (the Write tool refused report-style .md files in a subagent); its content is section 3 of the Recipe guide instead
Hull plates transfer only judged by eye; area test only 2 x 2; Blender 5.2.2 CPU only
dead_ends: Hough circles for rivets: nothing found; template matching worked
Area-threshold tracing (keep every patch above N dots): 6280 patches / 468 KB gave edge skill 0.51 on the preview; gain-per-byte got 0.58 with 300 KB
Palette 16 and 24 colours worse than 8 at the same bytes
Six shared edge profiles instead of 12 per-bar ones: edge skill 0.221 -> 0.164 (kept shared ones only for the sampler)
Half-dot misregistration and Blender tessellate_polygon failures cost ~0.04 SSIM / 0.05 edge skill until found; rejecting all self-touching outlines dropped the biggest patches (SSIM 0.717 -> 0.702)
Fine speckle layer written as colour layer swallowed the rust (15.6% -> 1.0%); first procedural wear far too fine (90 x 64 features)
Tuning for texture_compare with large-scale tone and less grain made the score worse (0.516 -> 0.454 -> 0.410); reverted
Real-geometry height / hybrid height did not help the match (geometry correlation 0.07 with reference height)
First random layouts: too many straps/braces in small panels, braces poking out of their panels (rectangle artefacts); fixed after look-and-fix round
Tried an edge 'sharpness' measure for the resolution test but scaled it wrongly; not reported
blender_tools_used: Python mesh (bpy.data.meshes, vertices/polygons, Color Attribute + point attributes)
Orthographic camera + Cycles (samples, box pixel filter), Standard/Raw view transform
Emission shader + Attribute node + Geometry node + Combine/Separate XYZ
Noise Texture 4D (seamless 'donut' feed via Math sin/cos nodes), Map Range, Math Multiply Add, Color Ramp (Constant), Mix (RGBA Mix/Multiply, Float), White Noise (grain)
Geometry Nodes: Curve Line, Quadrilateral, Curve to Mesh, Transform Geometry, Mesh Cone, Instance on Points, Realize Instances, Set Material
Blender MCP not needed; headless CLI Blender 5.2.2 used throughout
numpy/OpenCV analysis (k-means, template matching, rotate-and-count scans, autocorrelation)
changes_wanted_in_lib: description_audit.py: the 'grid' rule fires on any list of ragged outlines whose first five rows are longer than 64 numbers and on one 4800-number outline; check that rows have EQUAL length (a real grid) or count outline lists separately, so honest traced-outline descriptions do not need chunking
pixel_compare.py: option to ignore a band of N dots at the picture edge or to compare against a seam-healed reference (the reference's own seam makes border rows unfair)

texture_compare.py: the radial spectrum measure is normalised by total energy so one layer change moves every size; offer per-band raw distances; give the reference's own seam ratio (2.02) as an anchor for the seam measure

bake_harness / sweep_tools: sweep_tools only handles node groups with a Vector input; a generic 'sweep one number of a description through N values and bake' helper (like generator/make_sweeps.py) would help every surface
Add a documented half-pixel convention note (dot i spans i..i+1, outline through dot centres) and a preview-vs-Blender parity check helper to lib
